resolutions.rationale: The observable declaration state is shared by the pinned browser engines.
CSS Syntax accepts the EOF-recovered value; Chromium preserves the unclosed observable spelling while Firefox materializes closing parentheses.
The pinned browser engines expose modern rgb syntax through the shared legacy rgba serialization in CSSStyleDeclaration.
Typed property values expose the Chromium/WebKit canonical serialization after CSS Syntax EOF recovery; Firefox retains quotes around the recovered font-family string.
Chromium and WebKit remove unnecessary quotes around a simple font-family while Firefox retains them; SheetOM follows the measured Chromium fallback.
Chromium retains unclosed custom-property token structures, removes EOF comments, and replaces an escaped EOF with U+FFFD.
Chromium and Firefox replace the existing custom-property priority when setProperty is called without a priority, while WebKit retains !important; SheetOM follows the measured Chromium fallback.
Chromium retains the unclosed pending-substitution spelling while applying lexical EOF recovery such as comment removal.
The four adapted WPT subtests define the shared null and undefined conversion behavior.
Required WebIDL arguments throw TypeError before string conversion in the pinned browser engines.
A setProperty value is parsed independently and cannot escape into another declaration; invalid input leaves the previous declaration unchanged.
Custom-property method arguments retain their logical names and cssText escapes those names only when serializing CSS syntax.
The standard rule-tree operations and detachment identity are shared; the recovered padding spelling follows the existing Chromium fallback resolution.
Engines share expanded longhand ownership and prevent state resurrection, but background record order and omitted-component spelling diverge; SheetOM follows the pinned Chromium observation.
The pinned Chromium and Firefox engines accept the measured subgrid, anchor-size, contrast-color, and integer calc families with the same observable declaration state.
Chromium retains the incomplete pending-substitution spelling and supports target-text with a typed attr source while Firefox differs; both reject the measured leader and URL target-text cases.
The reviewed branches follow pinned Chromium where newer timelines are not shared across engines.

Chromium exposes expanded animation defaults and a different longhand order from Firefox and WebKit; SheetOM follows the pinned Chromium observable synthesis while preserving equivalent longhand semantics.
